outline.rationale: The user is a total beginner seeking conversational fluency, not building skills. I opened with a grounding definition node, then intuition for how AI "learns" (the single biggest conceptual gap for laypeople), then LLMs/chatbots since that's what most conversations center on today. The buzzword-untangling node targets the exact confusion beginners have (AI vs ML vs deep learning) which is essential for following discussions. Everyday-examples grounds abstractions in the familiar. The limitations and debates nodes equip the user to engage critically in real conversations — including hype, safety, and jobs, which are the actual talking points people raise. A vocabulary node acts as a reference so they can decode jargon. I deliberately excluded any coding, model-building, math, or tools nodes per the confirmed understanding, and avoided a history-of-AI node since it doesn't serve conversational fluency. Nodes are largely non-overlapping: definition, mechanism, application (LLMs), taxonomy, real-world presence, failure modes, societal debate, and terminology each answer distinct questions.
